title: The Re-Identification of Previously Unidentifiable Clinical Non-Tuberculous Mycobacterial Isolates Shows Great Species Diversity and the Presence of Other Acid-Fast Genera
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of clinical mycobacterial isolates, demonstrating significant species diversity through advanced molecular identification techniques and revealing the presence of previously undetected acid-fast genera in clinical samples.

title: High Prevalence of Prototheca Bovis Infection in Dairy Cattle with Chronic Mastitis in Ecuador
abstract: This study identifies Prototheca bovis as the primary etiological agent of chronic mastitis in dairy cattle in Ecuador for the first time. The research demonstrates a high prevalence (15.1%) of P. bovis infection in milk samples from cows with chronic mastitis, highlighting the significant economic impact on dairy production and the need for improved diagnostic protocols in veterinary bacteriology laboratories.

title: The Development of a Multiplex PCR Assay for Fast and Cost-Effective Identification of the Five Most Significant Pathogenic Prototheca Species
abstract: This study presents a multiplex PCR system (m-PCR) for accurate differentiation of the five most important pathogenic Prototheca species, including those associated with dairy cattle infections (P. ciferrii, P. bovis, P. blaschkeae, P. wickerhamii) and human infections (P. wickerhamii and P. cutis). The method is low-cost, using a simple heat-shock method for DNA extraction and requires only primers, Taq polymerase, agarose gel, and molecular weight marker for identification.

title: A rapid and inexpensive 96-well DNA-extraction method from blood using silicon dioxide powder (Glassmilk)
abstract: This study presents a rapid high-throughput DNA extraction method for use with EDTA-anticoagulated blood using silicon dioxide powder (SiO₂) as a guanidine-HCl solution, referred to as 'Glassmilk'. The method utilizes a 96-well deep-well plate, enabling DNA extraction from 96 samples in under 3 hours, integrating cell lysis, washing, elution, and DNA storage within the same well, eliminating the need for DNA transfer.

title: Addressing the Concern of Orange-Yellow Fungus Growth on Palm Kernel Cake: Safeguarding Dairy Cattle Diets for Mycotoxin-Producing Fungi
abstract: Palm kernel cake (PKC), a byproduct of palm oil extraction, serves an important role in Ecuador's animal feed industry. The emergence of yellow-orange fungal growth in PKC on some cattle farms in Ecuador sparked concerns within the cattle industry regarding a potential mycotoxin-producing fungus on this substrate. Due to the limited availability of analytical chemistry techniques in Ecuador for mycotoxin detection, we chose to isolate and identify the fungus to determine its association with mycotoxin-producing genera.

title: Shedding light on risk: Seroprevalence of Q fever among farm animals and workers in Ecuador
abstract: Serosurvey of farm workers, cattle, sheep and dogs on two Ecuadorian dairy farms using a commercial ELISA showed exposure to Coxiella burnetii (Q fever). Seroprevalence was 18% in farm workers, 30% in dogs, 25% in cattle and 2% in sheep. No association with abortion was found in cattle; however, high Neospora caninum seropositivity suggested a strong link to abortion. Results highlight Q fever circulation and occupational risk, underscoring the need for surveillance in animal and human health.

title: Bovine Papillomavirus Genotypic Diversity and a Putative Novel Viral Type in Ecuador
abstract: This study investigated bovine papillomavirus (BPV) type diversity in cattle from the Province Santo Domingo de Tsáchilas in Ecuador. Warty lesions were collected from 30 cattle across eight farms. Nucleic acids were extracted using a silicon dioxide-based method, and the partial L1 gene was amplified with PCR. DNA sequences were analyzed using maximum likelihood phylogenetics, identifying ten well-known BPV types and a putative novel viral type BPVEC2024-6-22-1 belonging to the genus Xipapillomavirus.
